messages:
Jules: :rotating_light: Pager alert - multiple inference containers on onprem-node-14 restarted 3x in the last 8m with kernel OOPS and CUDA illegal memory access. Seeing high paging activity and one node flap. Creating thread for coordination.
SRE-Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421. Severity: P1. Pager runbook: follow 'cuda-illegal-access'. Assigned: Priya (oncall).
Priya: taking this. digging in logs now. roughly when did it start?
Jules: first spike at 2119876400 (about 2m before alert), CPU stable, but dmesg shows device errors.
Marco: pasting dmesg snippet: ```
[2119876412.123] NVRM: GPU 0: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 80, Illegal Memory Access at 0x7f8c7a4b2000
[2119876412.123] kernel: CUDA: misaligned device address, addr=0x7f8c7a4b2000 len=4096
[2119876412.124] containerd: runtime created new task: infer-service-abc restart count=1
```
Priya: thanks. can anyone confirm if this is the same stack we saw in last week's pager?
Rafael: it's similar but stack trace differs slightly. looks like a kernel v5.15 hotpatching scenario + heavy paging. attaching truncated trace: ```
GPU kernel trace: nv_gpu_memcpy+0x1a4 
nv_map_user_pages+0x90 
user_thread_main+0x3f
```
Tess: customer-impact: two customers on the dedicated cluster reported elevated latencies and a failed request rate spike ~0.8% for the last 10m. no major data loss reported.
Jules: are there evac/fallback policies triggered? traffic should have failed over.
EngRuntime-Bot: Automatic fallback applied: model-variant-small deployed in region us-west-2 for traffic from onprem-node-14.
Priya: mitigation plan step 1: cordon node and shift new traffic. step 2: drain pods gracefully to avoid hot reloads. step 3: apply kernel param to disable a specific kmem feature if needed.
Marco: running `kubectl cordon onprem-node-14` now.
Priya: running `kubectl drain onprem-node-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`
SRE-Bot: Action log: node cordoned at 2119876482 by Marco. drain in progress.
Rafael: while draining, we saw 2 container restarts due to OOM in model shard loader. increasing swap pressure may be contributing. can we temporarily reduce max_batch_size to lower memory usage?
Jules: yes, reduce batch size via rollout: `PATCH /routes/infer-service/config { 'max_batch_size': 4 }`
Priya: patch applied and traffic rebalanced. monitoring token-level latency and error rate.
Marco: also noticed kernel message about userfaultfd and live-paging: `userfaultfd page-fault handled by kernel 0x3a`. suspect race between on-demand paging path and GPU DMA.
Tess: notified affected customers in incidents channel and CS is acknowledging. One customer asked for ETA; I gave ~30-45m while we stabilize.
Rafael: can we try hotpatch kernel param: `echo 0 > /proc/sys/vm/zone_reclaim_mode` on the node as a test? Might reduce kernel reclamation interference.
Priya: applying that on onprem-node-14 via ssh now.
Priya: applied. no immediate improvement, but crash frequency reduced from 1/min to 1/10m.
EngRuntime-Bot: Rollback candidate: deploy fallback-image with nvcc driver pin 470.82 for workers on node. Would you like to trigger a canary?
Jules: go ahead with canary on one drained secondary node first.
Marco: canary applied to onprem-node-15, no regressions for 10m.
SRE-Bot: Pager update: incident status changed to 'mitigating'. severity remains P1 until all nodes stable.
Priya: handoff note for next oncall: I will be handing over at 2119877000. Rafael, can you pick up next watch and continue the follow-ups (kernel debug, driver repro)?
Rafael: I got it. I'll continue kernel debug + coordinate with ML-eng for a repro.
Jules: summary for the customer-facing postmortem: root cause suspected kernel-userfaultfd + GPU DMA race triggered by high paging under memory pressure on onprem-node-14. Immediate mitigations: cordon/drain, reduce batch size, apply vm param, deploy driver-pin canary.
Tess: ETA for complete mitigation: once all drained nodes restart with pinned driver and no further OOMs for 60m. action item: open SEV ticket for engineering to investigate kernel race and reproduce in staging.
Priya: adding follow-ups in backlog: 1) capture full crash dump, 2) reproduce with stress workload + ufd, 3) test driver versions and kernel flags, 4) update runbook to include quick batch-size reduction.
Rafael: oncall note: I'll coordinate with EngRuntime and Eng-ML tomorrow 09:00 PT for deep-dive.
Jules: thx team. closing thread when all nodes pass 60m stability. :thumbsup:
